key_insight: A context-aware Markov decision model can tailor Type 2 diabetes follow-up intervals to patient risk, rather than using one fixed schedule for everyone.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help primary care teams schedule visits more efficiently by shortening follow-up for higher-risk patients and lengthening it for stable, well-controlled patients.
method: Used EHR data from 22,154 T2D patients across 10 primary care clinics.
Created patient contexts with PCA on health-trajectory variables plus clustering on principal components and patient features.
Learned CMDP policies for follow-up timing based on current lab status, recent hospitalization, and risk context.
evidence_signal: Compared with an ADA-like fixed-interval policy, the CMDP policy lowered expected cumulative cost by about 34.8% in the higher-comorbidity context and 6.4% in the lower-comorbidity context.
watch_item: The model was derived from retrospective EHR data, so real-world performance and fairness across settings would need prospective validation before use.
paper_title: Context-Aware Optimization of Follow-Up Intervals for Type 2 Diabetes Care Using Markov Decision Processes
